records.source: THE EVENT TYPE IS READ FIRST, and the liveness checks follow it. This filter is on the QApplication, so both `_still_alive` calls used to run for every event in the process -- 94,431 of them during one Regression open, and a profile counted the pair at 839,906 calls in one Mask open. This filter is on the QApplication, so both `_still_alive` calls used to execute for every event in the process -- 94,431 of them during one Regression open, and a profile counted the pair at 839,906 calls in one Mask open. Reading the type of an object whose C++ half has gone raises, which the `except` below already answers with the same `False`, so the order costs nothing and the checks now run only for a context menu.
records.translation: HÄNDELSETYPEN LÄSES FÖRST, och livskontrollerna följer efter. Det här filtret sitter på QApplication, så båda anropen av `_still_alive` kördes tidigare för varje händelse i processen -- 94,431 av dem under en enda öppning av Regression, och en profilering räknade paret till 839,906 anrop vid en enda öppning av Mask. Att läsa typen hos ett objekt vars C++-halva har försvunnit genererar ett undantag, vilket `except` nedan redan besvarar med samma `False`, så ordningen kostar ingenting och kontrollerna körs nu bara för en snabbmeny.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.gate_spec.ViewGate#2
records.source: THE VIEW IS PART OF THE GATE. An outline on the screen means nothing without the camera it was drawn through, so the gate carries the camera as ``projection``: a 4 x 4 matrix taking a measurement ``(x, y, z, 1)`` to homogeneous view coordinates ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, scaled so that ``sw`` is positive in front of the camera. The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved gate needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.
records.context: The view is part of the data-selection boundary. An outline on the screen means nothing without the camera it was drawn through, so the data-selection boundary carries the camera as ``projection``: a 4 x 4 matrix taking a measurement ``(x, y, z, 1)`` to homogeneous view coordinates ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, scaled so that ``sw`` is positive in front of the camera. The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved data-selection boundary needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.
records.translation: VYN ÄR EN DEL AV GATEN. En kontur på skärmen betyder ingenting utan den kamera den ritades genom, så gaten bär kameran som ``projection``: en 4 x 4-matris som tar ett mätvärde ``(x, y, z, 1)`` till homogena vykoordinater ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, skalad så att ``sw`` är positiv framför kameran. Konturen lever i ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rad ett, två och fyra är allt som :meth:`mask` behöver, så att tillämpa en sparad gate på nytt kräver inget plottbibliotek och ger samma svar på vilken dator som helst; djupraden låter bara konturen ritas tillbaka in i volymen från en annan vinkel.
